'''Alicia Prieto Langarica''' is an American applied mathematician and professor of mathematics at [[Youngstown State University]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://ysu.edu/faculty-experts/prieto-langarica-alicia|title=Prieto Langarica, Alicia|work=Faculty experts|publisher=Youngstown State University|access-date=May 10, 2021}}</ref>

==Education and career==
Prieto Langarica is the granddaughter of Mexican footballer [[Max Prieto]].<ref name=motivator/> She is a graduate of the [[University of Texas at Dallas]],<ref>{{cite web|url=http://vanguardstem.com/wcwinstem-alicia-prieto-langarica-ph-d/|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180409070912/http://vanguardstem.com/wcwinstem-alicia-prieto-langarica-ph-d/|archive-date=2018-04-09|title=#WCWinSTEM: Alicia Prieto Langarica, Ph.D. |date=July 9, 2017|work=Vanguard STEM}}</ref> and received her PhD in Applied Mathematics from [[University of Texas at Arlington]] in 2012. Her dissertation, ''From Discrete to Continuous Models of Cell Movement: An Application to Medical Implants'' was completed under the guidance of Hristo Venelinov Kojouharov.<ref>{{mathgenealogy|id=180354}}</ref>

She became an assistant professor of mathematics at Youngstown State University faculty in 2012, after she finished her doctorate.<ref name=motivator>{{cite magazine|url=https://ysu.edu/magazine/spring-2019/prieto-mathematician-motivator-mentor|magazine=YSU Magazine|publisher=Youngstown State University|date=Spring 2019|department=Our Faculty|title=Prieto: Mathematician, Motivator, Mentor}}</ref>

==Contributions==
Prieto Langarica's research focuses on the intersection of mathematics and biology, specifically problems related to the medical field.<ref name=faction>{{Cite web|title=Dr. Alicia Prieto Langarica|work=Faculty Faction|publisher=Youngstown State University|url=https://ysu.edu/people/alicia-prieto-langarica}}</ref>

She is one of four co-founders of Lathisms, a website that showcases Hispanic and Latinx mathematicians, their research, and their contributions.<ref>{{cite magazine|title="The Danger of a Single Story" in Mathematics: The Lathisms podcast shares the varied stories of Hispanic and Latinx mathematicians|magazine=[[Scientific American]]|first=Evelyn|last=Lamb|date=September 26, 2018|url=https://blogs.scientificamerican.com/roots-of-unity/the-danger-of-a-single-story-in-mathematics/}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|work=News & Events|publisher=Swarthmore College|date=October 14, 2016|first=Cody|last=McElhinny|url=https://www.swarthmore.edu/news-events/new-website-highlights-accomplishments-hispanic-latinoa-mathematicians|title=New Website Highlights Accomplishments of Hispanic, Latino/a Mathematicians}}</ref>

In 2019, she became one of the associate directors of [[Project NExT]], a program of the [[Mathematical Association of America]] to mentor new doctorates in mathematics.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://twitter.com/maanow/status/1113139307081076738|title=MAA is excited to welcome Dr. Alicia Prieto Langarica as the new associate director of #MAAProjectNExT!|date=April 2, 2019|publisher=Mathematical Association of America|via=Twitter}}</ref>

During the [[COVID-19 pandemic]], she organized events to give students food during shutdown,<ref>{{Cite web|title=Women Warriors Week Four: Dr. Alicia Prieto Langarica|url=https://www.cfmv.org/women-warriors-week-four-dr-alicia-prieto-langarica/|access-date=2021-04-09|website=Community Foundation of the Mahoning Valley}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|newspaper=Mahoning Matters|title=Alicia Prieto Langarica named this week's Women Warriors honoree: The associate professor at YSU worked with her network of friends and colleagues to collect food and essential items for the YSU Food Pantry, connecting international students stranded on campus with needed essentials|date=June 4, 2020|url=https://www.mahoningmatters.com/coronavirus/alicia-prieto-langarica-named-this-weeks-women-warriors-honoree-2406909}}</ref> focusing particularly on the needs of international students stuck in university housing.<ref>{{cite news|newspaper=Mahoning Matters|title=YSU professor serves as advocate for international students: "I was an international student, so I know how it can be hard and I know what things are difficult. It's not getting any easier," said Alicia Prieto Langarica, associate professor in the Department of Mathematics and Statistics|date=July 14, 2020|first=Alyssa|last=Weston |url=https://www.mahoningmatters.com/difference-makers/ysu-professor-serves-as-advocate-for-international-students-2560720}}</ref>

==Awards and honors==
Langarica won the [[Henry L. Alder Award]] for Distinguished Teaching from the [[Mathematical Association of America]] in 2019.<ref name=":14">{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=August 20, 2019|title=Excellence at Work: Math faculty earn state and national honors|url=https://ysu.edu/news/excellence-work-math-faculty-earn-state-and-national-honors|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=|website=Youngstown State University}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.maa.org/sites/default/files/pdf/awards/MathFest2019/Alder_PrietoLangarica.pdf|title=Henry L. Alder Awards: Alicia Prieto Langarica|work=MathFest 2019|publisher=Mathematical Association of America|year=2019|access-date=May 10, 2021}}</ref> She also won the 25 Under 35 Award in 2017, and was nominated for the Athena Award in 2019. She competed for five years in the Mexican Mathematical Olympiad, finishing in first place in two different years.<ref name=faction/>
